title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR Ultimo — mors spiritualis metaphorice / Luc 9:60
pass_a_gloss: GAR. Finally he argues thus. Spiritual death is death spoken metaphorically; corporal death properly. But who would think that in a law which ought to be conceived in most usual words, one and the same vocabulary-item ought to be taken at once both properly and metaphorically? especially since to die by death in a figured sense, I would not know to be taken, unless perhaps Luke 9:60.
pass_b_english: GAR. Finally he argues thus. Spiritual death is death said metaphorically; bodily death, properly. But who would think that in a law that had to be framed in the most ordinary words, one and the same term should be taken both properly and metaphorically at once—especially when I would not know 'to die the death' in a figured sense except perhaps at Luke 9:60?
source_text: GAR. Ultimo sic argumentatur. Mors spiritualis est mors metaphorice dicta; mors corporalis proprie. Quis autem existimet in lege, quae debuit verbis usitatissimis concipi, vocabulum unum, idemque debere accipi simul & proprie & metaphorice? praesertim cum morte mori figurato sensu, nescirem accipi, nisi forte Luc. IX. 60.
